HLP_Intro:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Introduction
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand>Pac-Man was born on May 22, 1980, at Namco in Japan,
$YEARS$ $YPLURAL$, $MONTHS$ $MPLURAL$ and $DAYS$ $DPLURAL$ ago.
Throughout its many editions, adaptations and tributes, its goals have always been the same:
Eat pacgums, survive, escape the ghosts or hunt them after gaining the superpowers of super-pacgums, collect bonuses, then start again on the next level.

This new installment builds on all these foundations... and adds a few more.
HLP_Principles:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Gameplay Principles
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>- Pac-Man eats pacgums and super-pacgums by moving over them.
- If the ghosts catch Pac-Man, he loses a life and reappears at the center of the level.
- If Pac-Man eats a super-pacgum, he becomes a ghost predator for a short time.
- If a ghost is caught, its spirit returns to its starting point, where it regains a tangible form.
- If time runs out, $TIMEOUTCONSEQUENCES$. This consequence can be configured in the settings.
- After eating all the pacgums in a given level, Pac-Man advances to the next level.
- Eating pacgums, ghosts or bonuses earns points.
- Every $NEWLIFEPOINTS$ points, Pac-Man gains an extra life. This amount can be configured in the settings.
- There is no cheat mode. Or perhaps there is. That information is not available here.
HLP_Interface:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Controls
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>The entire game can be controlled with a keyboard, mouse or gamepad, whichever you prefer. This guide shows the controls like this:
<justify=center><key=Keyboard key> <key=↑> <key=↓>     <mouse= > <mouse=leftclick> <mouse=left&right>     <pad=Gamepad button> <pad=↑> <pad=↓>

<justify=left>Some keyboard keys can be used interchangeably, such as:
<justify=center><key=↑> <key=←> <key=↓> <key=→>     <key=$SPACE$>     <key=$ESC$>
<key=$W$> <key=$A$> <key=S> <key=D>     <key=$ENTER$>        $ADDSPACE$<key=P>

<justify=left><font=regular><size=1><color=sand>Adjust the volume with <key=+> <key=->, <pad=Y> <pad=B>, or <mouse=wheel>.
Hold <key=Ctrl> or <pad=LT1> to adjust the music volume,
or <key=$SHIFT$> or <pad=LT2> to adjust the sound effects volume.

<key=F1> shows or hides tooltips, <key=Ctrl> <key=$SHIFT$> <key=B> toggles the banner, and <key=Ctrl> <key=$SHIFT$> <key=F> toggles the frame rate display.
<justify=right><font=italic><size=0.5><color=darksand>* these keys are displayed using the
layout corresponding to your keyboard.
HLP_Gamepad:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Gamepad
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>Here are the gamepad button labels used in this guide:
HLP_Menus:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Menus
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>You will encounter plenty of menus and other information throughout this game. At the very least, you have already discovered the main menu and this guide, and learned how to navigate them.
Everything else follows the same pattern: simple buttons, tooltips, and unavailable options shown in gray.

 You can use the keyboard <key=↑> <key=←> <key=↓> <key=→> <key=$SPACE$> <key=$ENTER$>,
the mouse <mouse=left&right&up&down> <mouse=leftclick>, or the gamepad <pad=⊙> <pad=A>.
Wherever possible, <key=$ESC$>, <key=$BACKSPACE$> or <pad=X> will take you back.

Animated text can be sped up with <key=$ENTER$>, <key=$SPACE$>, <mouse=leftclick> or <pad=A>.

Finally, if you really want to, you can always rage quit with <key=Ctrl> <key=C> or <key=Alt> <key=F4>, but you'll miss the chance to enter your name in the persistent leaderboards.
HLP_Settings:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Settings
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>Most game settings can be changed in the settings panel, and to a lesser extent from the pause screen during gameplay.
There you will find:
- the game language, tooltips, and idle time before the main menu screensaver starts
- display modes and the banner toggle
- audio volumes
- gameplay adjustments and the option to enable or disable mini-games

Each setting takes effect as soon as you select it and remains active while the game is running. You can also save your changes or restore the default settings.
HLP_Play:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Play
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>Once you've fine-tuned your settings, the Play button will take you into the game itself, with its epic tale, surprises, moments of joy, sorrow and frustration. Can you escape the curse of the Pac-Amama?

- To the left of the game board, you'll find your score, the current level, and your remaining lives. Remember, you can earn more.
- To the right, you'll find the time remaining to complete the current level (and if it seems short, there are ways to fix that), as well as your inventory.

Move Pac-Man with <key=↑> <key=←> <key=↓> <key=→>, <pad=⊙> or <mouse=left&right&up&down&leftclick>. Avoid the ghosts, learn their behavior, and eat every pacgum to complete the level.
The larger super-pacgums also let you eat the ghosts.
Everything you eat earns points, and points earn lives!

Pause the game and open its menu with <key=$ESC$>, <key=P> or <pad=MBR>.

From the main menu, you can also use <mouse=rightclick>, <key=$SHIFT$> <key=$ENTER$> or <pad=LT> <pad=A> on the Play button to access a specific level. Once completed, however, you'll return to the main menu.
HLP_Bonus:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Bonuses
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>During your adventure, you'll discover bonuses that can help you. They will be stored in your inventory and can be activated by clicking them <mouse=leftclick> or using their corresponding shortcut keys.
- the Hourglass, which turns elapsed time into remaining time   <key=1>    <pad=LBU>
- the Sage, which repels ghosts, though they remain dangerous   <key=2>    <pad=LBL>
- the Bomb, which clears corridors at right angles; beware!     <key=3>    <pad=LBR>
- the Life, which is immediately added to your reserve
- the Bow, which lets you change gender                         <key=4>   <pad=LT> <pad=LBU>
- the Stetson, which takes you into a wild world                <key=5>   <pad=LT> <pad=LBL>
- the Sticky Goo, which turns you into a hunted ghost           <key=6>   <pad=LT> <pad=LBR>

Whether you use them or not, collecting these bonuses earns points.
HLP_Minigames:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Mini-Games
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>Between certain conventional levels, Pac-Man's thoughts will lead you to other concepts in the form of mini-games. There are four, inspired by great classics:
- Pac-Snake
- Pac-Breaker
- Pac-Tris
- Pac-Invaders

Their rules will be explained before each one begins.
Points earned in these mini-games, and any extra lives gained from them, carry over throughout your game.

Mini-games can be enabled or disabled in the game settings.
When enabled, you can also launch them directly from the main menu's quick level selection using <key=$SHIFT$> <key=$ENTER$>, <mouse=rightclick> or <pad=LT> <pad=A> on Play.
HLP_Score:
<size=2><font=bold><color=yellow>Score
<size=1><font=regular><color=sand><justify=left>Your score increases as you play.
Whether you earn points by eating pacgums, super-pacgums or ghosts, collecting bonuses, or playing mini-games, those points earn you extra lives.
You currently gain one life every $NEWLIFEPOINTS$ points, and this threshold can be changed in the settings.

At the end of your game, whether you finish it or run out of lives, if your score deserves a place among the saved scores, you'll be able to enter your name or nickname.
There are two leaderboards: the Hall of Fame and the Wall of Shame.

<size=2><justify=center><font=italic>Which one would you rather be on?

<size=0.5><color=darksand><font=italique>Whatever your answer, we advise against trying to
tamper with the score file to improve your ranking.

Book of Platitudes
INT_026:
Apocryphal verses, lost, forgotten,
rediscovered, recycled as kindling,
and faithfully transcribed from memory

INT_051:
Yet another flativerse.

I've stopped counting them. I don't know if I'll ever get out.
My journey began $YEARS$ $YPLURAL$, $MONTHS$ $MPLURAL$ and $DAYS$ $DPLURAL$ ago.
It was stupid. Some old guy, a quest, a promise of adventure.

I should have listened to my mother.
Don't ask me what she said. I wasn't listening.
Who am I even talking to?

I'm going mad. All these flativerses, one after another, by the thousands,
by the millions, by the billions perhaps.
If anyone reads this, help me.
I want to get out of here.
INT_070: I saw a new object appear:
INT_071: I saw some new objects appear:
INT_082: the brown crate contained an hourglass
INT_083: the dark green crate contained a plant, perhaps sage
INT_084: the purple crate contained a bomb
INT_085: the red crate contained a hair bow, and I have no hair
INT_086: the white crate contained a hat
INT_087: the light green crate contained some sticky goo
INT_088: the yellow crate was empty, but I felt I had been given an extra chance
INT_092: Using the hourglass made me feel less pressed for time.
INT_093: The sage drove the ghosts away; they must hate the stuff.
INT_094: The bomb blast travels far down the corridors; it is dangerous for them and for me.
INT_095: I put the bow on my head, felt very different, and saw the world through rose-tinted glasses.
INT_096: I put the hat on my head, felt as though I had entered another reality, and the pacgums tasted metallic.
INT_097: The sticky goo covered me and carried me into another reality, where the pacgums tasted salty and creatures with strange appendages chased me.
INT_10102:
This flativerse was different.

Wider corridors, a strange layout, and I felt an odd
urgency to explore it, as though my time was running
out.

I don't know what to make of it, but after decades
of wandering through identical flativerses, this
change gives me hope. Could these differences mean
my exile is finally coming to an end?

My friend Phil used to say:
"Anything different is good."
INT_10203:
The peculiarities of the previous Flativerse were also
present in the one I just crossed. I really hope this means
the exit is getting closer. It would be dreadful to have
travelled from Flativerse to Flativerse for over $YEARS$ $YPLURAL$
only to reach another region just as long.

Let's see what this one has in store for us.

”Us”? I must remember I'm alone here.
Alone with those ghosts.

Referring to oneself in the plural is hardly a sign of
sound mental health, I'm afraid...
INT_10304:
Sometimes I'm surprised to find time to... daydream.

And yet I'm almost constantly being chased, and I still
feel that strange sense of urgency ever since the
Flativerses started changing.
Perhaps I'm simply uncomfortable with change.

I don't sleep, either. And yet I'm not tired.
Perhaps I'm put to sleep when I'm moved from one
Flativerse to another.
How could I possibly know? There's no way to measure
the passage of time objectively here. All I know is
the time I spend awake, and from that I estimate the length
of my exile. I keep repeating it to myself so I won't forget.

I am a prisoner.
INT_10405:
The Flativerses are getting bigger.

I hardly dare believe this is another sign that the
way out might be getting closer and closer.

The old man who recruited me for this adventure spoke of
Flativerses extending into a dimension we normally cannot
access, the fourth. I didn't understand a word of it.
My world gets along perfectly well with its two physical
dimensions and its one-way dimension of time, thank you very much.
Who would want an extra dimension, and what would they do with it?

But if the Flativerses are growing, perhaps it means they
have more room in that other dimension, that they're spreading apart...
And that might mean the way out is near.

I want to believe it.
INT_10506:
I've been thinking again about the passage of time and how to measure it.
There is no sun in these Flativerses. No way to
measure a day.

Sometimes I miss it. I loved feeling its light and warmth,
even though it was so far away, resting in the plane,
tracing its circle without ever wavering.

Here, there is light without a sun. I have no idea where
it comes from, but I can see perfectly well. That isn't normal.

I hope I'll see the sun again.
INT_90001:
Pacgums.

That's all I've eaten since my journey began.
Ghosts, for their part, are hardly nutritious.

Despite my misfortune, I'm lucky. Pacgums have perfect
nutritional properties and are metabolized completely.
Fortunately so, because Flativerses have no restrooms,
and I could never afford to stop long enough to relieve myself.

Sometimes, when I'm not in immediate danger, I wonder
what my life would be like if my body had to store
food waste, even temporarily.

How much could I hold? Would I risk exploding?
INT_90002:
The ghosts.

The old man said they would be here, that they're actually
projections of the consciousness of multidimensional entities.

I didn't understand any of that gibberish. Multi means two, right?
So we're all multidimensional.

They hunt me. They never stop, or at least not for long.
They're present in every Flativerse.

I hate them for their relentlessness, their cruelty, their stupidity
too. Every time I get back up, their inexorable hunt begins
again, as though they had no other purpose than to torment me.

I dream of vengeance, of revenge, of retribution.
I dream of destroying them all.
I dream of justice.
INT_90003:
Where do the ghosts come from?

Every time I arrive in a flativerse, they're already there.
According to the old man, they're not the same individuals but
countless identical copies originating from four entities
existing outside these flativerses. And indeed, there are always
four of them, never more, never less.

I wonder if there are other types, with different colors
and different behaviors.
Are they mass-produced, then stored somewhere until they're
put into service?

My uncle Alexey runs a warehouse.
His favorite joke is that if we lived in a lineverse,
that is, a flativerse with only one dimension, moving a crate
around would be almost as difficult as in his warehouse.

Uncles aren't always funny.
INT_90004:
I've been thinking about those ghosts that might be stored
in large numbers somewhere.

In a way, I'm lucky.
I only encounter four of them in each flativerse, and they're
not particularly bright.
Except the pink one, who anticipates my movements.
And the cyan one, who tries to flank me.
And the orange one, who has realized this hunt is pointless,
pretends to join the others, then runs away from me.
But the red one! What an idiot!

Thank goodness there are only four of them.
I'd stand much less of a chance if they attacked in a swarm.
What could I do then?
Spit pacgums at them?

MGO_Gnr:
Mini-Games

Mini-games punctuate Pac-Man's journey as he ponders his situation.
Each mini-game is preceded by instructions explaining how to play.

Not all these games use the same controls: you may need
the <key=keyboard>, the <pad=gamepad>, or the mouse <mouse= >.
You can always pause with <key=$ESC$>, <pad=MBR>,
or by clicking <mouse=leftclick> the button at the bottom left.

Points earned in mini-games carry over throughout your game, as do the extra lives they earn you.

Enjoy the game!
SNK_Htp:
Pac-Snake

Guide Pac-Snake toward pacgums and super-pacgums, and watch it grow longer until it fills the entire board!
Avoid the edges and Pac-Snake's own body.

Steer its head with <key=↑> <key=←> <key=↓> <key=→> or <key=$W$> <key=$A$> <key=S> <key=D>,
or with the gamepad <pad=⊙>.

Once moving, Pac-Snake never stops.
Set Pac-Snake in motion to begin.
BRK_Htp:
Pac-Breaker

Destroy the ghosts on the board using Pac-Man. Once the board is cleared, it will rebuild itself and Pac-Man will speed up.

Use the paddle to aim and bounce Pac-Man. Your reserve of Pac-Men is shown at the bottom of the screen.
Depending on their color, ghosts may take several hits to disappear.
Bonuses may drop when ghosts are hit. Catch them to discover their effects.

Move the paddle with <key=←> <key=→> or <key=$A$> <key=D>,
the gamepad <pad=↔>, or the mouse <mouse=left&right>.
Aim with <key=↑> <key=↓> or <key=$W$> <key=S>, the gamepad <pad=↕>,
or by holding the mouse button <mouse=leftclick&left&right&up&down>.
Launch with <key=$SPACE$> or <pad=A>, or by releasing the mouse button <mouse=leftclick>.

The game ends when you lose your last Pac-Man.
TRS_Htp:
Pac-Tris

Arrange groups of four ghosts into horizontal rows to clear them from the board.

As you progress, the groups will fall faster and faster.
The 'Next' column lets you anticipate upcoming groups.

Move groups with <key=←> <key=→> or <key=$W$> <key=D>,
or with the gamepad <pad=↔>.
Rotate them with <key=$SPACE$> or <pad=A>.
Make them fall faster with <key=↓> or <key=S>, or <pad=↓>.
Swap with the held group using <key=↑> or <key=$W$>, or <pad=↑>.
Switch the horizontal movement mode with
<key=Ctrl> + <key=$SPACE$> or <pad=LT> + <pad=A>.

The game ends when no new group can enter the board.
NVD_Htp:
Pac-Invaders

Survive successive waves of ghosts by firing pacgums at them.

They will attack you too, each wave will be faster than the last, and reinforcements will arrive.
Fortunately, you have several lives, displayed at the bottom of the screen, defensive barriers to protect you, and occasional bonuses dropped by hit ghosts to help you out.

Move Pac-Man with <key=←> <key=→> or <key=$A$> <key=D>, the mouse <mouse=left&right>, or the gamepad <pad=↔>. Fire with <key=$SPACE$>, <pad=A> or <mouse=leftclick>. You can also hold the fire control.
Without a bonus, you can only have one projectile in flight at a time.

The game ends when you run out of lives or the ghosts overrun your defensive line.
